title: Emotion Recognition in Human-Robot Interaction
summary: As robots transition from industrial settings to human-centric environments—such as homes, clinics, and classrooms—their ability to perceive and respond to human emotions has become a cornerstone for effective interaction. Emotion recognition enables robots to go beyond mere task execution, allowing for more natural, adaptive, and meaningful engagement. The evolution of affective computing, multimodal sensing technologies, and intelligent behavior modeling has propelled the integration of emotional intelligence into robotic systems. However, challenges remain in interpreting complex human affect, especially in real-world, culturally diverse, and ethically sensitive contexts. To advance these capabilities, a deeper interdisciplinary collaboration among robotics, neuroscience, psychology, and AI is essential. This Research Topic aims to explore the state-of-the-art in emotion-aware robotics and its transformative potential across domains.

Leadership for Emerging Technologies in Schools: Roles of Educational Leaders in Driving Digital Innovation

Their rapid incorporation into educational systems demands new leadership approaches capable of guiding pedagogical innovation, supporting teachers’ digital competence, and ensuring safe and ethical implementation. Research shows that teachers and headmasters or other types of leaders play a decisive role in whether emerging technologies are meaningfully adopted or remain underused. Yet current studies often focus either on technology or on leadership separately, leaving a gap concerning how both interact to influence school transformation. This Research Topic aims to address this gap by exploring how educational leadership shapes, enables, or restricts the integration of emerging technologies in schools.

title: Gender, Emotions, and Artificial Intelligence
summary: The intersection of gender, emotions, and artificial intelligence (AI) is a rapidly growing area of research. AI systems, now ubiquitous, are not neutral; biases in training data and design decisions can inadvertently perpetuate societal inequalities and harmful stereotypes. This is particularly evident in affective AI, which seeks to recognize and respond to human emotions, and in applications like facial recognition where disparities based on gender and skin tone have been observed. Understanding these biases and their consequences is crucial as AI increasingly influences aspects of daily life. Research aims to identify and mitigate these biases, ensuring AI benefits all members of society equitably. title: Improving decoding of neuroinformation: towards the diversity of neural engineer, Volume II
summary: The Central Nervous System (CNS) provides information about how individuals collect information from their surroundings, how they process that information to make decisions, and finally, how they behave and act in their environment. CNS information can be gathered from three main sources: (1) electrical currents (e.g., electroencephalography – EEG) or electrocorticography (ECoG)), (2) magnetic fields (e.g., magnetoencephalography – MEG), and (3) level of blood oxygen or blood flow (e.g., functional near infrared spectroscopy – NIRS or functional magnetic resonance imaging – fMRI). This neuroinformation is being decoded to develop neural interfaces that aim to establish, re-establish and/or improve the neural interconnectivity of CNS in order to optimize the human-environment interaction. Not only decoding of neuroinformation has been pursued so far, but also finding the best way to recode neuroinformation by brain stimulation has been of interest in the scientific community.

title: Computational mechanisms of sensory and multisensory integration in perception and action
summary: While considerable progress has been made in mapping sensory and multisensory processing at behavioral and neural levels, key questions remain regarding the computational rules and neural implementations underlying integration. How does the brain weigh and combine inputs with varying reliability? At what stages and under what conditions are signals fused versus maintained separately? How do these processes differ between perception and action, and which neurobiological mechanisms are shared or distinct? This Research Topic aims to bring together interdisciplinary investigations that combine neurophysiology, psychophysics, computational modeling, and artificial intelligence to reveal new insights into the computational principles governing multisensory integration. By synthesizing experimental, theoretical, and applied approaches, we seek to clarify how the brain manages sensory uncertainties and coordinates perception with flexible, goal-directed action.

title: Developing Musical Expression, Communication, and Wellbeing

Music can be used to enhance wellbeing in various contexts, including health care settings and as a tool for social impact. Musical expression and communication have the potential to enhance people's sense of wellbeing; however, this does not happen automatically and can be particularly challenging for those studying or working within the music profession. Therefore, it is vital to explore the variety of processes involved in developing musical expression and communication that enhance wellbeing for all involved. These processes include (but are not limited to) psychological, educational, and artistic domains.

title: Perception in Virtual Worlds: Sensorimotor Contingencies, Perceptual Illusions, and Presence
summary: Immersive VR and XR now allow perceptual science to be conducted under rich, interactive conditions that approximate everyday sensorimotor engagement better than conventional screen-based paradigms. However, virtual worlds are not neutral containers: presence, embodiment, and agency can amplify attentional capture and reshape perceptual judgments, while device optics, latency, locomotion interfaces, and haptic realism can introduce systematic biases. As a result, findings obtained in virtual environments may diverge from classic laboratory outcomes in both magnitude and mechanism. A coherent research agenda is needed to explain when immersion improves ecological validity, when it compromises inference, and which design and measurement practices yield reliable and reproducible perception research in virtual worlds.

summary: Within human neuroscience, recent advances have transformed our perspective on depression and anxiety, reframing them as conditions of network-level dysfunction rather than isolated regional brain disturbances. The field is grappling with how these dysfunctions interact transdiagnostically, predict clinical heterogeneity, or evolve across the lifespan. title: History of Animal Behavior Sciences: Behavioral Natural History and Comparative Psychology in the period 1500-1975
summary: Scholars have devoted attention to animal behavior since Antiquity. One of the first was the Greek philosopher Aristotle, who described, for instance, the waggle dance of honeybees, the courtship kissing of pigeons and the parental transmission of singing behavior in songbirds. However, while there were notable naturalists in Antiquity, Middle Ages and Renaissance, it is only from the 17th century that animal behavior sciences underwent a steep growth. Historically, a wide variety of scholars contributed to animal behavior, under different labels, each of which has become a field of its own. In particular, in the period 1500-1975, three main fields contributed to the development of animal behavior science: natural history, comparative psychology and ethology.

Authenticity is emerging as one of the most important factors that we value in leaders, as difficult decisions to be made often test leaders’ core beliefs, which allow stakeholders to see if a) leaders’ actions are aligned with their beliefs, and b) leaders’ beliefs are aligned with those of employees, the organization, and other relevant stakeholders. title: Peers as Bridges to Belonging: Fostering Community Through Near-Peer Mentorship in Large-Enrollment Courses
summary: Large-enrollment courses are a defining feature of undergraduate education worldwide, yet they pose well-documented psychological challenges for both students and instructors. These threats are magnified for students from historically underrepresented backgrounds, including first-generation college students, racial and ethnic minorities, and students navigating identity-based stereotype threats. In response, institutions have increasingly turned to peer-led instructional models—undergraduate teaching assistants, learning assistants, supplemental instruction leaders, and peer mentors—as a strategy for humanizing large courses and creating more supportive learning environments.

title: Embodied Approaches to Intervention and Research Design in Clinical Psychology: Integrating Body, Context, and Measurement
summary: Clinical psychology has long recognized that psychological distress and therapeutic change involve more than cognitive processes alone. Emotion regulation, symptom expression, trauma responses, and treatment outcomes are shaped by bodily states, autonomic function, interoceptive awareness, and the lived contexts in which clients exist. Yet clinical research methods can overlook these embodied dimensions. Treating physiological variability, posture, breath, circadian timing, and relational dynamics as clinically meaningful variables can bring further insight into treatment and management pathways. When embodied dimensions are not systematically incorporated into research design and measurement, this can limit the precision of assessment, weaken treatment specificity, and contribute to unexplained variance in clinical outcomes.

title: Virtual reality as a tool for cognitive and sensory modulation
summary: Virtual Reality (VR) has emerged as a transformative medium in neuroscience, moving beyond entertainment into a robust tool for experimental manipulation. Traditionally, studying cognitive and sensory processes required a trade-off between controlled laboratory settings and real-world ecological validity. VR bridges this gap by providing immersive, three-dimensional environments that can be precisely modulated to isolate specific neural responses. title: Intrinsic neural dynamics and information processing in decision-making circuits
summary: Decision neuroscience is a rapidly advancing field aimed at understanding how neural circuits give rise to behavioral choices. However, vital questions remain about how spontaneous activity patterns and network fluctuations influence the reliability, adaptability, and efficiency of cognitive operations leading up to a choice. In particular, we still lack a clear understanding of the neural dynamics that govern the transition from an evidence accumulation state to the commitment to a specific choice, a key step in the decision process.

title: Current Perspectives of The Neurobiology of Prosody and Rhythm
summary: Prosody and rhythm are core components of speech that allow the brain to transform acoustic signals into linguistic and affective meaning. title: Unraveling the Neuropsychological Ground of Substance-Related and Non-Substance-Related Addictive Behaviors
summary: Modern neuropsychology views addiction as the behavioral consequence of neuroadaptation including notably maladaptive recalibration of the reward system from "liking" (hedonic pleasure) to "wanting" (compulsive craving), a breakdown in executive control and abnormal emotional processing. The state of the art in addiction neuropsychology has shifted from a simple "dopamine rush" theory to a complex neuro-circuitry model characterized by multiple structural and functional brain reorganization. Neuropsychology considers both the risk factors and the consequences of addictive behaviors, with an interest on recovery and the reversibility of neurobiological process. Based on the heterogeneity of profiles, the field is moving toward individual neuropsychological phenotyping, including cognitive, behavioral and emotional abilities, which would allow us to stratify patients and provide personalized and adapted care.

title: Timing the senses: From auditory temporal coherence to audiovisual integration
summary: Human perception operates within a chaotic sensory environment, where the brain must constantly determine which signals arise from the same source. A critical mechanism for this is temporal coherence, being the degree to which different sensory features fluctuate together over time. In the auditory domain, temporal coherence is a primary driver for stream segregation, allowing the brain to bind diverse frequencies into a single "object." However, this principle extends beyond audition. Temporal structure serves as a fundamental organizing principle for perception across sensory modalities, acting as a "glue" that helps the brain determine which signals belong together. While we understand that timing is important for both auditory grouping and multisensory binding, the precise transition from intramodal temporal coherence to intermodal audiovisual integration remains a complex challenge in human neuroscience.

title: Mechanisms and Effects of Music Education on Learning and Wellbeing in Childhood and Adolescence

Recent advances—spurred by large-scale initiatives such as the WHO-commissioned review by Fancourt and Finn (2019)—have integrated epidemiological findings, classroom-based interventions, and mechanistic research. title: The Influence of Spiritual and Religious Practices on Mental Health and Psychological Resilience
summary: Within the field of health psychology, there is growing recognition of the importance of psychosocial factors such as spirituality and religiousness (S/R) in shaping mental health outcomes. Despite a longstanding debate, recent evidence points toward both beneficial and adverse effects of S/R practices on psychological well-being. Some studies highlight how spiritual or religious engagement can provide individuals with meaning, purpose, and feelings of belonging, which serve as protective factors against mood disorders and psychological distress. Conversely, other research points to potentially negative consequences arising from rigid belief systems, religious struggles, or experiences of exclusion and existential doubt. The complex relationship between S/R and mental health is further complicated by cultural, contextual, and individual differences, underscoring the need for more nuanced and integrative research in this area.

title: Cognitive–motor interactions in aging: neural mechanisms, behavioral signatures, and functional consequences
summary: The fields of motor control and cognitive psychology have been traditionally separate, but research has fundamentally reshaped this distinction. We now understand that motor control and cognitive functions are inextricably linked, sharing neural pathways and competing for limited resources, especially in aging. As neural efficiency declines in aging, there is a tradeoff between using resources to support motor performance and cognitive function. For example, older adults often display reduced performance on complex tasks due to cognitive-motor interference, compared to younger adults. Understanding the mechanisms behind this shift is critical for distinguishing between healthy aging and early-stage neurodegeneration. It will also facilitate the development of interventions aimed at preserving functional independence.

title: (Re-)Theorizing the Psyche: Exploring Foundational Shifts in Psychological Science
summary: The replication crisis has exposed deep-seated tensions within psychological science. Beyond technical or procedural flaws, it has raised fundamental questions about the epistemic architecture and ontological assumptions of the discipline. While most responses have focused on methodological refinement, such as improved statistical tools, preregistration, or open science initiatives, these efforts often leave unexamined the more foundational question: what the replication crisis reveals about psychological theory and about the assumptions psychology makes about its object of inquiry, the “psyche” beyond technical procedure.

title: Sensory-motor integration in human movement
summary: For desired and coordinated movements, the central nervous system integrates multiple sensory feedback with motor commands. Compromised sensor-motor integration can potentially lead to a stability control deficiency, increased risk of falling, tremors, rigidity, and decreased hand dexterity, just to name a few. However, there is a limited understanding of the mechanisms responsible for sensory-motor integration, specifically, how the central nervous system adapts to changes in environmental conditions (e.g., visual input is obstructed), physical and mental health, and cognitive status. A comprehensive study of sensory-motor integration can be beneficial to healthcare professionals, neuroscientists, and human health in general.

title: Artificial Intelligence for Medical Robotics: From Design Acceleration to Intelligent Perception and Control
summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly transforming the field of medical robotics, extending its impact beyond traditional perception and control to earlier stages such as system design and modeling. Emerging approaches leverage machine learning to accelerate computationally intensive processes, including finite element analysis (FEA) for soft and continuum surgical robots and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for medical devices such as blood pumps. In parallel, data-driven methods provide effective alternatives to analytical modeling for complex robotic systems with challenging kinematic and dynamic structures. These advances complement ongoing developments in AI-enabled perception, planning, and intraoperative decision-making. Together, they create new opportunities for improving the efficiency, intelligence, and clinical applicability of medical robotic systems, while also introducing challenges in reliability, interpretability, and integration.

Along this rapid development, multi-agent systems are expected to achieve multi-modal fusion representation at the cognitive level, enable proactive exploration at the learning level, and enhance task allocation, resource sharing, and collaborative coordination at the team level.

title: Future of Theoretical and Philosophical Psychology
summary: Psychological science is at a crossroads. The last two decades has brought a range of fundamental issues into focus, including the replication crisis highlighted by large-scale community efforts such as the Open Science Collaboration, problems with representativeness and diversity emphasized by researchers such as Apicella, Norenzayan, and Henrich, and concerns regarding the very nature of the construction of theories raised by Oberauer and Lewandowsky; and van Rooij and Baggio, and more recent contributions by van Dongen and colleagues. At the same time, long-standing questions about explanation, evidence, and mind-world relations are now intersecting with rapid developments in cognitive science, neuroscience, and artificial intelligence. These converging trends highlight both the urgency and the opportunity for rigorous theoretical and philosophical work that can clarify, critique, and guide the future of psychology.

title: Interdisciplinary Approaches to Literacy Acquisition and Disorders: Neuroscience, Psychology, and Education
summary: Literacy acquisition and related disorders stand at the intersection of neuroscience, psychology, and education, forming a convergent field that investigates how brain systems support the development of literacy skills. Recent research has greatly advanced our understanding of the neural and cognitive substrates underlying reading, highlighting the complex interplay between speech perception, phonological processing, orthographic knowledge, and language comprehension. Yet, significant questions remain regarding how these processes coalesce to foster successful reading development and precisely how disruptions in these systems lead to disorders such as dyslexia. Notably, gaps persist in mapping the developmental trajectories of brain networks for reading, elucidating cross-linguistic differences, and translating mechanistic insights into practical frameworks for intervention and education.

title: Music and the Brain: From Neural Mechanisms to Clinical Applications
summary: The field of music neuroscience explores how music engages complex brain networks, making it a uniquely powerful tool for investigating neural processes that underpin perception, action, emotion, prediction, and reward. Recent advances in neuroscience demonstrate that music activates widespread brain systems, from the auditory cortex to motor and reward networks, enabling the study of core principles such as neural entrainment, oscillatory timing, and predictive processing. Large-scale, multimodal studies have begun to illuminate how music can serve as both a model for basic brain function and as a pathway for understanding neurological and psychiatric disorders. Yet, critical gaps persist in linking circuit-level findings to clinically meaningful outcomes, elucidating moderators across development, and leveraging music as a precision tool for diagnosis and intervention.

summary: The capacities of awareness, selection, and sustained attention are critical for human communication, from an adult perceiving speech sounds and comprehending complex discourse, to an infant babbling surrounding speech sounds and associating new words with their meanings. When the brain is functioning atypically, due to developmental differences or an injury, the demands of linguistic processing can heavily tax attentional resources. A growing body of research highlights that deficits in one domain frequently co-occur with, and profoundly influence, impairments in the other. Understanding this dynamic interplay is important for advancing our theoretical models of typical human speech and language, and for developing more effective diagnostic and therapeutic strategies for a wide range of developmental and acquired speech and language disorders.

title: Transforming Genitourinary Surgery Through Advanced Robotic Systems
summary: The field of genitourinary (GU) surgery has undergone a transformative shift with the integration of robotic technology, which now serves as a cornerstone for minimally invasive procedures. Over recent decades, advancements have evolved from pioneering platforms like PUMA 560 and Probot to current industry standards, exemplified by the da Vinci system. Robotic approaches have been lauded for improved dexterity, enhanced visualization, and better ergonomics for surgeons, leading to increasing adoption. Despite their technical promise, clinical debates remain around appropriate patient selection, comparative benefits over other minimally invasive modalities, and the economic implications of broader deployment. Although early evidence points to advantages such as reduced blood loss and faster recovery, critical gaps persist, including inconsistent outcome definitions, limited long-term data, and a lack of standardized benchmarks for both clinical and technical success.

title: Bioactive phytochemicals with neuroimmunopharmacological properties
summary: Plants constitute a vast and still incompletely characterized reservoir of biologically active compounds. Among them are highly potent therapeutic agents such as paclitaxel, employed in oncology, and morphine, a cornerstone of severe pain management. Moreover, numerous plant-derived products contain complex phytochemical compositions that contribute to the maintenance of physiological homeostasis and may play a preventive role in the early stages of disease development. Accordingly, plant-derived substances – including crude extracts, enriched fractions, or isolated compounds – may be considered as valuable candidates for the development of therapeutics, dietary supplements, or functional food components. In any case, these substances exert measurable biological effects by modulating physiological functioning and molecular pathways.

AI in Human Neuroscience, Ethically Done: Neuroethical Risks, Safeguards, and Governance
summary: Artificial intelligence is revolutionizing human neuroscience, enabling unprecedented advances in brain imaging analysis, neural decoding, predictive modeling, and personalized neurological interventions. However, the rapid integration of AI into neuroscience research and clinical applications raises critical ethical concerns that remain inadequately addressed. These include privacy vulnerabilities with neural data, algorithmic bias in brain-based diagnostic tools, issues of informed consent in AI-driven neuroscience studies, and the potential misuse of neural information for non-medical purposes. As AI systems become increasingly sophisticated and widely deployed, there is an urgent need for comprehensive frameworks that balance scientific innovation with robust ethical safeguards. This Research Topic brings together neuroscientists, ethicists, technologists, and policymakers to advance the responsible integration of AI in human neuroscience.

title: Advancing Critical Military Suicide Studies: Challenging Assumptions and Innovating Prevention
summary: Suicide among military servicemembers and veterans is a profound and persistent public health challenge, manifesting across national and cultural contexts. Despite systematic surveillance, targeted research, and significant resource allocation over the past two decades, suicide rates within military and veteran populations have increased or remained elevated in many Western countries. Historically, efforts have concentrated on the identification of risk and protective factors, the development of clinical interventions, and the implementation of broad institutional prevention strategies. While substantial advancements have been made in clinical, policy, and programmatic domains, a deep-seated paradox persists: investments in conventional prevention strategies have not consistently produced meaningful reductions in suicide deaths or been sufficiently responsive to the unique needs of the military and veteran community, highlighting gaps in our theoretical and practical approaches.

title: Neuroscience of learning: How the brain adapts and changes, Volume II
summary: The human brain is remarkably dynamic, constantly adapting to new experiences and environmental changes. This plasticity underlies our capacity to learn throughout the lifespan, shaping how we acquire knowledge and develop new skills. Recent advances in neuroscience have illuminated the cellular, molecular, and network-level changes that support learning, revealing a complex interplay between genetic, neurochemical, and experiential factors. Understanding these mechanisms provides crucial insights into cognitive development, educational strategies, and interventions for learning disorders, making the neuroscience of learning a vibrant and relevant field of research.

title: The Future of Brain Imaging: Techniques and Applications
summary: Brain imaging technologies have been instrumental in advancing our understanding of neural structure, function, and connectivity. Established techniques such as MRI, fMRI, PET, and EEG have provided invaluable insights into brain organization and dynamics in both health and disease. However, the field is rapidly evolving with the emergence of innovative imaging modalities and methodological refinements. Next-generation approaches—including ultra-high field imaging, multimodal integration, real-time imaging, functional ultrasound, and AI-enhanced analysis pipelines—promise unprecedented spatial and temporal resolution. These advances are expanding the frontiers of what we can measure and understand about the human brain, while simultaneously presenting new challenges in data interpretation, standardization, and clinical translation. This Research Topic explores the current state and future trajectory of brain imaging science.

title: The interplay between economic and biopsychosocial factors in brain health
summary: Financial well-being is a strong determinant of human. Individuals from lower socioeconomic backgrounds encounter a disproportionate amount of chronic stress, limited access to resources, and reduced opportunities for cognitive stimulation, all of which can profoundly influence brain development and functioning across the lifespan. At the same time, biological factors (e.g., genetic and biomarker-based risk factors), cognitive function and numerical abilities, and mental health variables like depression and anxiety, can influence an individual's ability to acquire and manage financial resources. There is likely a reciprocal relationship between financial well-being and the brain. Despite growing interest in this field, the bidirectional mechanisms linking economic factors to brain functioning, and health remain poorly understood.

title: Translational research of occupational therapy and psychiatric rehabilitation, Volume IV
summary: The field of occupational therapy (OT) has long recognized the importance of addressing mental health issues to improve overall well-being and functionality in individuals. Despite significant advancements, there remains a critical gap between basic scientific discoveries and their practical application in clinical settings. This gap underscores the need for translational research in the mental health domain of occupational therapy. Translational research serves as a bridge, facilitating the transfer of knowledge from fundamental research into real-world therapeutic interventions that can be effectively utilized by practitioners and benefit patients.

title: Beyond the Average Brain: Person-Specific Mechanisms and Within-Person Prediction
summary: Traditional neuroscience research has relied on group-level analyses, identifying average patterns across populations. However, substantial heterogeneity exists in brain structure, function, connectivity, and neurobiology across individuals. This variability is not merely noise but reflects meaningful differences in genetics, development, experience, and biology that shape cognition and behavior. Person-specific (idiographic) approaches and within-person prediction models recognize that individuals follow unique neural trajectories and respond differently to interventions. Recent advances in computational modeling, machine learning, intensive longitudinal designs, and single-subject neuroimaging enable detailed characterization of individual brain patterns and their behavioral correlates. Precision neuroscience—tailored to the individual—promises more accurate prediction, more effective interventions, and deeper mechanistic understanding of brain-behavior relationships.

title: Neuroactive microbial metabolites and human brain function: mechanisms, biomarkers, and clinical implications
summary: In the rapidly evolving field of neurogastroenterology, mounting evidence highlights the profound influence of neuroactive microbial metabolites on human brain function. The gut-brain axis has become a focal point for understanding how metabolites produced by gut microbiota, reshaped by factors such as diet, medications, and stress, interact with the central nervous system. Recent studies have delineated pathways by which short-chain fatty acids, tryptophan metabolites, bile acids, and other molecules alter blood–brain barrier integrity, microglial activation, neurotransmitter systems, and neural connectivity. Despite promising insights, critical questions remain regarding the reproducibility of findings, individual susceptibility, and translation to clinical practice. There remains a significant gap in mapping specific metabolite signatures to neuropsychiatric phenotypes, as well as understanding how genetic and environmental factors modulate these effects.

title: Safety Critical Intelligent Control of Systems with Uncertain Dynamical Models
summary: Intelligent control has become a cornerstone of modern robotics and autonomous systems, where agents must operate safely and reliably despite uncertainty in their dynamics, environments, and sensing. However, achieving formal safety and stability guarantees within such frameworks remains a crucial and unsolved challenge. Uncertainties due to unmodeled dynamics, sensor noise, or real-time learning processes can threaten mission-critical reliability—especially when systems must make autonomous decisions without human oversight.

title: Multisensory interactions in speech and language: from theory to application
summary: Speech and language perception are inherently multisensory processes. The integration of auditory, visual, and somatosensory signals plays a fundamental role in how humans process and produce language across the lifespan. Despite significant advances in cognitive neuroscience, psycholinguistics, and computational modelling, key questions remain regarding the neural mechanisms underlying multisensory speech integration, how these processes break down in clinical populations, and how they can be harnessed in real-world applications.

title: Psychological Health and Safety at Work: A Systems-Level Approach to Psychosocial Risk, Organizational Context, and Employee Well-Being
summary: Psychological health and safety (PHS) has emerged as a critical priority in contemporary workplaces, reflecting growing recognition of psychosocial risks such as excessive workload, job insecurity, and poor organizational support. Traditionally, research on employee well-being has focused on individual-level stress and coping; however, there is increasing emphasis on organizational and system-level determinants of mental health at work. Frameworks such as the Job Demands–Resources (JD-R) model and psychosocial safety climate (PSC) highlight how work design, leadership, and human resource practices shape both risk and protective factors. Recent developments, including international standards such as ISO 45003, further underscore the need for integrated approaches to managing psychological health and safety. This Research Topic builds on this shift by examining how organizational systems create, sustain, or mitigate psychosocial risk and influence employee well-being.

title: Resilience and Psychological Recovery in Times of Stress and Uncertainty: Pathways to Mental Health and Human Flourishing
summary: The field of psychological resilience and adaptation has gained increasing relevance in recent years as individuals and societies face persistent stressors ranging from global crises to personal hardships. Research has illuminated the complex interplay between biological, psychological, and social processes that underpin human responses to adversity. Despite an expanding body of evidence, questions remain about how people rebuild wellbeing after disruption, the mechanisms that sustain recovery, and the factors that distinguish mere survival from genuine flourishing. Emerging studies challenge traditional deficit-oriented frameworks and instead highlight dynamic models of growth, flexibility, and meaning-making. Yet, gaps persist in understanding how contextual, cultural, and temporal factors influence the trajectories of psychological recovery and personal development.

Socially Assistive Robots (SARs), in particular, have been explored in therapeutic and educational settings, suggesting positive effects on engagement, communication and socio-emotional development, especially among vulnerable populations such as children with autism. The rise of synthetic opioids and polysubstance use, the explosion of behavioral and digital addictions (gaming, social media, gambling), and breakthrough treatments once considered fringe — such as GLP-1 receptor agonists and psychedelic-assisted therapies — have transformed both the questions we ask and the tools we use to answer them. title: Next-gen neuro-AI: Aligning foundation models and biologically plausible architectures with human cognition
summary: Cognitive computational neuroscience has entered a transformative era. The rapid rise of large multimodal foundation models, state-space architectures, and advanced transformers has shifted the conversation: we are no longer just building artificial intelligence to solve tasks, but actively using these models as candidate mathematical "theories of the mind." By comparing the latent representations of artificial neural networks with biological neural activity, researchers are uncovering unprecedented insights into human perception, memory, decision-making, and language.

title: Sleep to Think: Multimodal Mechanisms Linking Sleep, Learning, and Performance
summary: Sleep is not merely a passive state but a dynamic process fundamental to learning, memory consolidation, and cognitive performance. During sleep, the brain undergoes remarkable transformations—reorganizing neural circuits, strengthening newly acquired memories, and clearing metabolic waste accumulated during wakefulness. Decades of research have established that adequate sleep enhances learning capacity, improves problem-solving, and optimizes performance across academic, athletic, and professional domains. Conversely, sleep deprivation impairs attention, working memory, and executive function. Yet the precise multimodal mechanisms linking sleep architecture, electrophysiological activity, neurochemical processes, and behavioral outcomes remain incompletely understood. Recent advances in polysomnography, neuroimaging, electrophysiology, computational modeling, and biomarker assessment have enabled more sophisticated investigation of sleep-dependent learning and performance. title: Reimagining Human Movement: The Impact of Extended Reality on Physical and Emotional Experience, Volume II
summary: Extended Reality (XR), encompassing Virtual, Augmented, and Mixed Reality, has rapidly moved from novelty to a credible tool for shaping how humans learn, train, recover, and express movement. Volume I of this Research Topic attracted broad engagement across motor learning, neurorehabilitation, sport performance, and creative movement, confirming a vibrant interdisciplinary community working at the intersection of immersive technology and human physicality. It also exposed three areas where the evidence base remains thin: durable, long-term effects of XR-based movement training; applications across the full lifespan, in particular healthy aging and clinical populations; and inclusive, equitable design of immersive movement experiences. Volume II builds directly on this momentum, deepening the scientific conversation rather than restarting it, and broadening the contributor pool toward clinical, developmental, and applied settings.

title: Brain–body interactions in neuropsychiatric and neurological disorders
summary: Understanding the complex communication between the brain and peripheral systems has become central to human neuroscience. Recent research highlights that the central nervous system interacts dynamically with the immune, endocrine, cardiovascular, and gastrointestinal systems, influencing both brain function and behaviour across the lifespan. Dysregulation in these bidirectional networks is increasingly implicated in the development and progression of neuropsychiatric and neurological disorders such as depression, schizophrenia, Parkinson’s disease, and Alzheimer’s disease. Emerging evidence from neuroimaging, multi-omics, and clinical studies underscores the role of systemic inflammation, metabolic dysfunction, and gut–brain signalling in shaping cognitive and emotional processes. Despite these advances, a comprehensive understanding of how brain–body interactions contribute to the onset, progression, and treatment response of these disorders remains incomplete. title: Multimodal data integration for precision brain health
summary: Breakthroughs in human neuroscience have enabled the generation of diverse and high-dimensional data from genomics and epigenomics, advanced neuroimaging, fluid and digital biomarkers, as well as cognitive and behavioral assessments. Despite these advances, single-modality studies often fall short in capturing the complexity of brain health and disease, leaving gaps in our understanding of nervous system development, mechanisms underlying neuropsychiatric and neurological conditions, and factors affecting brain aging. Recent research has demonstrated the potential of integrating data across multiple biological and behavioral domains to uncover novel biomarkers, patient subtypes, and mechanistic insights. However, challenges remain around analytic integration, clinical translation, and ensuring reproducibility and equity in findings.

Pushed to Choose: Motivational, Emotional, and Physiological Processes in Police Decision-Making
summary: Police decision-making often unfolds in emotionally charged, uncertain, and time-pressured environments. Officers are required to interpret ambiguous cues, regulate affect, assess risk, and act in ways that are lawful, proportionate, and operationally effective. Yet these decisions are not shaped by cognition alone. Emotional states, chronic occupational stress, fatigue, burnout, trauma exposure, moral strain, and psychological well-being can all influence attention, judgment, impulse control, communication, and post-incident recovery. At the same time, the consequences of police decisions extend beyond individual performance to public trust, procedural justice, use-of-force outcomes, and officers’ long-term mental health. A focused discussion of how emotional processes and well-being interact with police decision-making is therefore timely and necessary, both for psychological theory and for evidence-informed practice.

title: Translational brain imaging–guided neuromodulation
summary: The intersection of advanced neuroimaging and neuromodulation is reshaping how we understand and treat disorders of the nervous system. Techniques such as transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS), transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS), deep brain stimulation (DBS), and focused ultrasound have matured considerably over the past two decades. Yet their clinical impact has remained constrained by a fundamental gap: stimulation protocols are rarely informed by the individual’s brain structure and function. Neuroimaging is poised to close that gap. By mapping functional connectivity, cortical excitability, white matter architecture, and network-level dynamics, we can now move beyond one-size-fits-all approaches and toward precision neuromodulation grounded in the living brain’s own organization.

summary: The boundaries between work and non-work life have never been more blurred. As hybrid arrangements consolidate as the dominant model in knowledge-intensive sectors, employees increasingly move between professional and personal domains — often within the same physical space. While hybrid work offers autonomy and flexibility, growing evidence suggests it also reshapes the psychological mechanisms through which employees disengage from work, recover from daily demands, and protect their well-being. In this context, the rapid evolution of digital tools and the pervasiveness of communication technologies have introduced new complexities, making individual coping strategies to manage digital demands and psychologically detach from work a critical area of investigation.

title: Edge AI for Robotics: Emerging Technologies and Applications
summary: Edge AI enables AI models to run directly on local devices, bringing computation closer to data sources for faster, more efficient decision-making. Therefore, it is critical for modern robotics, where rapid and robust decision-making is essential. In applications such as high-speed drones and industrial robots operating in extreme conditions, on-device processing ensures real-time control and reliability. Moreover, as service robots become increasingly integrated into daily and personal environments, preserving user privacy during data processing is paramount. While recent advances in AI and deep learning have significantly enhanced robotic capabilities in perception, decision-making, and control, relying solely on cloud-based processing can introduce delays and compromise privacy. Leveraging edge AI enables decentralized, real-time computation that meets the demanding requirements of today's robotic applications.

Recent advances emphasize the interplay between high-level cognitive mechanisms and neural processes, particularly during real-time social interactions. How do oscillatory brain activities support the mechanisms of joint attention, and how does interbrain synchrony reflect interpersonal coordination beyond shared perceptual input? summary: Human motor system executes the motor command from high-order regions, rigorously controls the musculoskeletal system and learns to adapt to novel stimuli of dynamic environments. Due to the highly redundant characteristics of the motor system, understanding the optimal and individualized principles of motor control and motor learning is still a scientific challenge. Understanding how brain controls motion and how musculoskeletal system performs commands from the brain and interacts with physical world is a focus for basic science, engineering and clinical translation.

summary: Liberated from the rules, obligations, and pressures of daily life, yet standing at its very core, play promises absolute freedom and happiness not only to humans but also to animals. Allowing us to become both actor and spectator, play is perhaps the ultimate safe haven where we soothe our existential anxieties. The Vygotskian understanding of play constitutes a central context in which children develop abstract thinking and self-regulation, internalize speech through the transition from social to private and inner speech, and demonstrate their learning potential within the zone of proximal development. title: Brain Organization and Behavioral Asymmetries: From Sensory Processing to Cognition Across Species
summary: The two hemispheres of the brain are neither structurally nor functionally symmetrical, and these asymmetries are often reflected in behavior. For more than a century, it was a common but mistaken belief that lateralization was unique to the human brain. However, it is now well established that hemispheric asymmetries are fundamental components of sensory, cognitive, and motor systems across vertebrates and many invertebrates. Behavioral measures such as motor preferences and perceptual biases provide valuable tools for investigating these processes, reflecting links between observable behavior and neural organization. Evidence across taxa also suggests that hemispheric asymmetries may confer evolutionary advantages by enhancing neural efficiency and supporting perceptual, cognitive, and motor performance, with potential benefits for survival.

In the context of increasingly sedentary lifestyles and growing cognitive demands, understanding how the body influences the brain is more important than ever. A central concept in this field is neuroplasticity, as physical exercise may induce structural and functional changes in the brain that support cognitive function and resilience against aging and neurological decline.

summary: Recent advances in robotics are increasingly driven by the integration of intelligent algorithms, advanced sensing technologies, and novel actuation mechanisms. In particular, the emergence of soft robotics has introduced new opportunities for safe and adaptive interaction with complex environments, enabled by compliant materials and innovative actuation methods e.g., pneumatic actuators. At the same time, progress soft sensor technologies such as optoelectronic sensors has enhanced proprioception capabilities, while machine learning and model predictive control have improved decision-making and system performance. Improving Vision-Guided Robotic Systems Through Next-Generation Hand-Eye Calibration Techniques
summary: Robotic vision systems form the foundation of modern industrial automation, enabling high-precision tasks such as assembly, inspection, and object manipulation. Central to their performance is hand-eye calibration, which defines the spatial relationship between the robotic manipulator and the visual sensor. Traditional calibration methods typically rely on multiple feature points, complex mathematical transformations, and iterative optimizations, increasing the risk of cumulative errors and computational inefficiencies. Recent approaches leveraging simplified configurations—such as single fixed feature point methods and algorithms like Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) and Levenberg-Marquardt (LM)—have shown promise in reducing setup complexity. However, persistent issues with accuracy, robustness to sensor noise, and adaptability to dynamic environments highlight the need for innovative solutions that balance precision with operational efficiency.

title: Nutritional neuroscience: How sensory signals influence diet and cognitive function
summary: Despite growing awareness of the role of nutrition in health and cognitive function, the intricate neural mechanisms linking sensory signals and dietary behavior remain underexplored. Sensory cues like taste, smell, and texture significantly influence food preferences, portion control, and satiety, yet how these signals interact with brain regions involved in reward, decision-making, and memory is not fully understood. This gap in knowledge limits our ability to develop effective interventions for nutritional challenges such as obesity, eating disorders, and age-related cognitive decline.

title: Rehabilitation Robotics: Clinical Effectiveness and Patient Engagement
summary: Medical robotics is entering a new phase of development, one in which technological innovation is increasingly expected to translate into meaningful benefits for patients’ recovery, participation, and overall wellbeing. In rehabilitation, robotic systems are no longer viewed only as tools for assistance or repetition, but as part of broader care pathways that can support motivation, autonomy, continuity, and personalized intervention. At the same time, patient engagement has become a central concern in the design and implementation of effective rehabilitation strategies. Advances in wearable and assistive robotics, soft systems, intelligent sensing, remote care, and digital health integration are creating new opportunities to connect physical rehabilitation with more responsive and patient-centered models of support. This Research Topic aims to explore that growing convergence and to highlight contributions that can shape the next generation of rehabilitation-oriented medical robotics.

Together, these constructs have been used to help explain why the degree of brain pathology does not always correspond directly to the severity of its clinical manifestations.

Optimizing Health and Well-Being Across the Lifespan: A Multidimensional Health Psychology Perspective
summary: Across modern life and work contexts - characterized by uncertainty, complexity, and accelerating demands- sustaining human performance and well-being has become both a psychological and public health priority. Human Performance Optimization (HPO) offers a unifying framework that views optimal functioning as the outcome of dynamic interactions among cognitive, emotional, physical, social, and spiritual domains. Originally rooted in performance-critical settings such as the military, HPO has evolved into a multidimensional approach relevant to healthcare, education, sport, and organizational life. Within health psychology, this paradigm resonates with holistic and positive health models that emphasize resilience, adaptability, and meaning as pillars of sustained human effectiveness and flourishing. Despite growing interest, there remains a need to better understand how these interwoven processes promote lasting well-being and to translate them into evidence-informed practices.

title: Edge-Deployed Generative AI for Context-Aware Decision Support in Wearable Robotic Systems
summary: Recent advances in Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI), particularly large language models (LLMs), have transformed how machines interpret, reason, and communicate. title: Effort, Attention, and Arousal: Brain–Body Mechanisms for Performance in the Real World
summary: Sustained performance in high-stakes, real-world environments places extraordinary demands on the human brain and body. Effort, attention, and arousal are three tightly interwoven constructs that together govern how individuals mobilize cognitive and physiological resources to meet these demands. Nowhere is this more critical than in contexts in which humans are expected to perform in high stakes environments. For example, military personnel, first responders, and individuals of the like must maintain peak cognitive performance under conditions of extreme stress, fatigue, sensory overload, and physical exertion. Despite decades of laboratory research, the neural and peripheral mechanisms underpinning the interaction between mental effort, attentional control, and arousal remain incompletely understood — particularly in the demanding and ecologically complex environments that are present in real-world scenarios.

title: From Mechanism to Management: Neuropsychological, Neurobiological, and Psychopathological Foundations of Geriatric Psychiatric Care
summary: Geriatric psychiatry sits at the intersection of neuroscience, psychology, and clinical medicine, addressing the complex mental health challenges that accompany aging. Older adults often present with multifactorial conditions, including depression, anxiety, cognitive decline, psychotic symptoms, medication effects, and sleep disruption, that rarely conform to a single explanatory level. Recent research highlights complex interactions among neurobiological changes, psychopathological presentations, psychopharmacological treatments, and psychosocial variables such as loneliness and autonomy. Despite growing evidence, clinical care models often remain fragmented, with limited integration between neuropsychological assessment, biological mechanisms, and treatment approaches. This integration gap underscores the need for a translational, multidisciplinary framework spanning the continuum from neuropsychological and neurobiological mechanisms to psychopathology and treatment in later life.

title: Predictive motor control and internal models
summary: Skilled motor behaviour relies on the central nervous system’s capacity to predict, rather than merely react to, the sensory consequences of its own actions. From reaching for a cup of coffee to maintaining balance on a moving train, every voluntary movement relies on the central nervous system’s ability to anticipate the sensory consequences of its own actions. This predictive capacity is thought to be supported by internal models: neural representations of the body and the external world that allow the brain to estimate forthcoming states and select appropriate motor commands. Forward models predict the sensory outcomes of motor actions, while inverse models compute the motor commands required to achieve a desired sensory or kinematic goal. Together, they form the computational backbone of skilled, flexible, and adaptive behaviour, and their disruption is increasingly recognised as a hallmark of several neurological and psychiatric conditions.

summary: Cognitive processes such as attention, perception, memory, executive function, and social cognition emerge from dynamic interactions between distributed neural systems. While correlational methods like neuroimaging and electrophysiology have mapped these networks extensively, they cannot establish whether a given neural signature is necessary or sufficient for a cognitive function. Causal interventions—including non-invasive brain stimulation (TMS, tDCS, tACS), pharmacological manipulation, and closed-loop neurofeedback systems—offer a powerful complement, allowing researchers to directly perturb neural systems and observe the behavioral consequences. Advances in real-time signal processing and adaptive stimulation now make it possible to test cognitive theories with unprecedented precision and mechanistic specificity.

ME/CFS is characterized by persistent and unexplained fatigue, post-exertional malaise, cognitive impairments, and a range of other symptoms such as pain, sleep disturbances, and gastrointestinal issues. Despite the significant impact on patients' lives and the number of sufferers, ME/CFS remains poorly understood, stigmatized, and lacks effective treatments.

Emerging evidence suggests that maternal factors during pregnancy — including physical activity, nutrition, stress, and metabolic and immune profiles — play a crucial role in shaping the offspring’s neuropsychological outcomes. title: Enhancing Brain Health: Physical, Cognitive, and Nutritional Interventions
summary: Brain health reflects the dynamic interplay of neural development, plasticity, and resilience across the lifespan. Emerging evidence shows that physical activity, cognitive engagement, and nutritional status each exert powerful, and often synergistic, effects on brain structure and function. These influences extend from early neurodevelopment through healthy ageing, and shape vulnerability to neuropsychiatric and neurodegenerative conditions. At the same time, environmental exposures, genetic background, and lifestyle factors interact in complex ways that remain incompletely understood. Within clinical neuroscience, there is a growing need to clarify how targeted interventions in these domains can promote optimal nervous system development, preserve cognitive function, and mitigate disease risk. This Research Topic will integrate mechanistic, translational, and clinical research to delineate how physical, cognitive, and nutritional interventions can enhance brain health.

A notable limitation is the ability to perform contact-rich, fine-grained, and high-precision manipulation, crucial for real-world applications. Recent studies highlight a need for learning-based approaches, multimodal perception, and hierarchical planning strategies to overcome these barriers, aiming to improve dexterity and autonomous capabilities. Progressive efforts in the field have seen the rise of foundation models and visual-language-action models that integrate perception and action, allowing for nuanced manipulation tasks.

title: Enhancing safety and resilience in autonomous robotic systems: Addressing complexity with integrated AI and cybersecurity solutions.
summary: Autonomous robotic systems are increasingly evolving across diverse domains, including manufacturing, healthcare, autonomous vehicles, and space exploration. These systems' growth in autonomy and deployment in intricate and sometimes hazardous settings highlights the pressing need for their safety, security, robustness, and reliability. Historically, robotics heavily relied on deterministic control and pre-set behaviors, but the integration of machine learning, particularly deep learning, has ushered in more adaptable decision-making capabilities. Despite these advancements, new challenges emerge concerning unpredictability, explainability, and vulnerability to faults and cyber threats.

title: Ergonomics of Recovery: Enhancing Mental or Cognitive Workload Relief and Well-Being in Contemporary Workplaces
summary: The field of workplace ergonomics has expanded rapidly in response to the cognitive, emotional, and physical demands of contemporary work environments, particularly as organizations adopt digital and hybrid modalities. In this context, mental workload—often used interchangeably with cognitive workload—refers to the psychological demands placed on attention, memory, and executive control during task performance. Advances in technology have increased flexibility and connectivity but also intensified risks of mental workload accumulation, psychological strain, and blurred work-life boundaries. Prolonged digital exposure, multitasking, and reduced restorative breaks can undermine employee well-being and performance. These challenges highlight the need to translate ergonomic and human factors principles into practical strategies that foster cognitive recovery, inclusivity, and sustainable organizational effectiveness.

summary: The ocean plays a critical role in the well-being of all humans on the planet, yet in many ways, we are still just at the beginning stages of ocean exploration. Recent advances in several areas of marine research and technology as well as in the social sciences have the potential to re-envision how we work within the ocean, ranging from telepresence via robots to direct observation via brief visits using crewed submersibles to living on the seafloor using saturation diving. Yet the full potential of these methods to fully engage the non-scientific public requires a new paradigm for how Western societies live and work as part of the ocean, ideas envisaged using cutting-edge methods of storytelling such as film and serious games, and informed by multiple non-Western cultures.

summary: Focus, the grammatical means of highlighting information to convey meaning and intention, is a fundamental component of human communication, critical not only for oral interaction but also for advancing natural human-machine interfaces. Cross-linguistic research reveals profound diversity in how languages employ prosody, syntax, and semantics to mark focus, offering a window into language typology and evolution. At a neurocognitive level, focus processing is intimately linked to attention and prediction mechanisms, with neural correlates (e.g., activity in the superior temporal gyrus) being identified for intonational contours. Despite significant progress, an integrated understanding of focus across theoretical, experimental, and applied domains remains elusive.

title: Multimodal stimulation techniques
summary: Traditional neuromodulation techniques, such as transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) or transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS), have revolutionized our ability to non-invasively probe and alter brain activity. However, single-modality approaches often face inherent limitations in achieving highly specific or sustained effects due to the brain's distributed nature and compensatory mechanisms. A new frontier is emerging at the intersection of various stimulation methods and sensory inputs: multimodal stimulation. By combining distinct neurostimulation techniques (e.g., electrical, magnetic, optical, acoustic) with or across various sensory domains (e.g., visual, auditory, somatosensory), we can potentially unlock more sophisticated and targeted modulation of neural circuits, leading to enhanced understanding of brain function and more effective therapeutic interventions.

title: New Perspectives on the Role of Sensory Feedback in Speech Production: Volume IV
summary: Speaking represents one of our most complex motor behaviors, one that is vital to our ability to communicate. To understand how speech is produced, one crucially important question to address is: how is sensory feedback used in the speech production process? Answering this question is an important step to understanding how the motor skill of speaking is initially learned and then maintained, as numerous studies have shown that sensory feedback plays a key role in these learning processes. There is also evidence that sensory feedback is important for successful moment-by-moment control of ongoing speech output. It is natural, therefore, that significant portions of current models of speech production are devoted to explaining the role of sensory feedback. Furthermore, abnormal processing of sensory feedback appears to be involved in many disorders of speech and voice production, like laryngeal dystonia and stuttering.

title: Predictive Coding: From typical cognition to clinical conditions
summary: Predictive Coding (PC) is a prominent theoretical framework that posits that a core function of the brain is a hierarchical inference process. It actively generates predictions about the causes of sensory input and continuously updates these based on "prediction errors" (the mismatch between expectation and reality). This parsimonious model offers a mechanistic account for a wide range of typical cognitive functions, from basic sensory inference and perceptual stability to motor control and decision-making.

title: Resource‑ and Energy‑Aware Multi‑Robot Operations: Scheduling, Recharging, and Long‑Horizon Persistence
summary: Battery capacity, recharge logistics, and computational budgets are now the primary bottlenecks for scaling multi robot systems from short demos to dependable, 24/7 operations. Long horizon missions—warehousing, inspection, agriculture, environmental monitoring, and public safety—require fleets to coordinate tasks, routes, and recharge events while accounting for battery aging, stochastic demand, uncertain travel times, and heterogeneous platforms. Classical planning or perception advances alone are insufficient: persistence hinges on resource models, predictive energy usage, and infrastructure aware scheduling that closes the loop between algorithms, chargers, and the physical environment. This Research Topic focuses on the algorithmic and systems foundations that make multi robot autonomy sustainable and economically viable over days to months, emphasizing measurable mission availability, throughput, safety under energy constraints, and total cost of ownership.

title: Robotic advancements in healthcare: Achieving complex medical tasks through precision and adaptability
summary: In recent years, healthcare has been witnessing an increasing integration of robotic systems, underscoring their growing potential to carry out complex medical tasks with unprecedented precision, safety, and adaptability. Medical robots are now increasingly utilized in various applications, such as assistant robots for tasks like sterilization, patient monitoring, and medical imaging; rehabilitation systems, including exoskeletons and smart prosthetics; as well as procedural robots deployed in surgeries and minimally invasive interventions. While these technologies often offer redundant degrees of freedom, enhancing their flexibility and dexterity in constrained environments, they also present notable challenges in kinematics, control, and real-time decision-making. Addressing these challenges is crucial, as higher precision is essential to inspire confidence among patients and medical staff alike.

title: Robotics and AI in the Hospitality and Service Industries

These innovations are reshaping how businesses operate and engage with their customers and employees. Robotics and AI bring the promises of enhancing customer experiences and optimizing operational efficiencies across various hospitality and service sectors. Yet, the hospitality and services industries have been slow to embrace technology. Labor experts predict that in the next few years these industries will change rapidly bringing significant shifts in hospitality and service industry tasks and jobs. AI is similarly predicted to transform service experiences.

title: Robust Reinforcement Learning Methods and Applications in Robotic Perception-Cognition-Decision Systems
summary: In recent years, reinforcement learning (RL) has demonstrated great potential in robotic tasks such as perception, control, and autonomous decision-making, becoming a key driver of robotics and embodied intelligence. However, deploying reinforcement learning policies from simulation to the real world (sim-to-real) often requires extensive hyperparameter tuning to accommodate varying tasks and dynamic environmental conditions. As robots gradually transition from controlled laboratory settings to open, dynamic real-world environments, they are increasingly confronted with challenges such as perceptual noise, environmental disturbances, and model discrepancies. These factors significantly limit the generalization and robustness of current RL methods. Therefore, improving the robustness of reinforcement learning algorithms in robot systems has become a key issue that urgently needs to be addressed.

title: Searching for the timekeeping center in the brain
summary: Time recognition presents a unique conundrum within the realm of neuroscience, as it lacks dedicated sensory organs and relies on brain mechanisms distinct from other senses. Contemporary research and neuroimaging studies have illuminated a network, including the prefrontal cortex, parietal cortex, and cerebellum, as integral to subjective time perception. While attempts to pinpoint a central timekeeping hub continue, understanding time perception's involvement across various neurological and developmental disorders, such as autism or ADHD, remains essential. This field of research holds potential to unravel the complexities of time recognition in the brain, driving us closer to identifying the elusive "center" of temporal processing.

Sentient AI: Myth, Reality, or Future Opportunity?
summary: The question of whether artificial intelligence can achieve sentience has evolved into a critical area of exploration in psychology, philosophy, and technology. AI sentience refers to the capacity of an AI system to experience subjective consciousness and feelings. Understanding this phenomenon requires addressing key aspects such as the development of reliable indicators for detecting sentience, the theoretical frameworks of consciousness that may apply to AI, and the limitations of AI in replicating human or animal experiences. Recent advances in cognitive science and deep learning have shed light on consciousness theories, enhancing our understanding of potential AI sentience. As we consider deeper into this topic, critical questions arise: What does the potential for AI sentience reveal about our own consciousness? How close are we to realizing sentient AI, and what moral implications would it imply?

title: The human neuroscience of music therapy in neurological and psychiatric disorders, Volume II
summary: Music therapy has long been recognized for its therapeutic benefits across a variety of medical conditions, including mental health disorders, developmental disabilities, and physical rehabilitation. In recent years, there has been a growing interest in understanding how music therapy can specifically benefit individuals suffering from neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, and Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS). Music therapy might engage and activate neural pathways that remain functional in patients, offering cognitive, emotional, and social advantages when other forms of interaction might fail. However, while the anecdotal and preliminary evidence is promising, comprehensive neuroscientific research that elucidates the mechanisms behind these benefits remains sparse.

A comprehensive understanding of mental disorders requires insight into both the underlying biological deficiencies and the maladaptive psychological processes and behavioral dysfunctions. This is achievable through translational research, which bridges fundamental research findings with clinical applications, thereby contributing to the overall improvement of healthcare and the industry.

title: Trust Dynamics in Digital Media: Personality, Politics, and Psychological Underpinnings
summary: The field of media psychology has increasingly focused on the complex interplay between individual characteristics and digital ecosystem structures in shaping political information processing and trust. While initial optimism predicted that digital platforms would democratize discourse, current evidence indicates that social media often exacerbates polarization, misinformation, and the fragmentation of public opinion. Recent research has shifted toward unpacking the psychological mechanisms that guide users’ engagement, with particular attention to enduring personality traits and their interaction with algorithmic recommendations and persuasive digital architectures. Despite extensive documentation of growing distrust and the proliferation of misinformation online - which is only set to increase with the growth of genAI - critical gaps remain in understanding how and why trust in digital media is differentially constructed across populations.

title: Virtual Bodies for Real Humans - Avatars, Sensations and Emotions
summary: Our bodies are fundamental to how we experience and interact with the physical world, and they shape the way our minds develop. The human brain develops together with the rest of the human body, adapting to its specific properties like size, weight or the resulting biomechanics. Virtual/extended reality (VR), on the other hand, allows us to instantly assume a virtual body (avatar) of any kind. While virtual bodies do not need to follow real-world physical, anatomical or biomechanical constraints, their users are humans whose brains are wired to represent human bodies. VR enables embodiment in entirely new forms—human, animal, robotic, or abstract—raising profound questions: How does our human sensorimotor experience shape interactions in non-human avatars? How can we create realistic sensations and emotional expressions for virtual bodies?

title: Women in Aging Neuroscience: new perspectives and challenges
summary: The study of aging is currently a central theme for society, as in 2024, the global life expectancy at birth reached 73.3 years, reflecting an increase of 8.4 years since 1995. The global population aged 60 and older is expected to rise from 1.1 billion in 2023 to 1.4 billion by 2030 (World Health Organization). Although aging is stereotypically associated to negative traits, studies have shown that neural plasticity is possible during the entire lifespan and that physical and cognitive performance can be maintained in the elderly within biological constraints.
